subject: mathematics
question_text: Find the vector equation of the plane passing through the points i − 2j + 5k, −5j − k and −3i + 5j.

recall_prompt: Say the vector equation of a plane through three given points.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Name the three points
steps.margin_note: First mark. Three points fix a plane. Watch the gaps: the second has no i term and the third has no k term — write those components as 0 rather than leaving them out.
steps.memory_tip: Mind the gaps: the second point has no i and the third has no k. Write those components as 0.

recall.must_convey: That the three given vectors are named as position vectors a, b and c of three points on the plane.
accept: name the three points a b and c
call the three position vectors a b c
three points determine the plane, name them
moodu points ni a b c ani peru pettali

steps.why: Two points give a line; three give a plane. The count of points is what selects the two-parameter form below.
common_mistakes: Missing a zero component when copying a vector.
Using only two of the three points.

steps.label: Write the equation
steps.margin_note: Second mark. A plane needs TWO parameters, s and t, because it is two-dimensional. The three coefficients (1−s−t), s and t always add to 1.
steps.memory_tip: A plane needs TWO parameters because it is two-dimensional, and the three coefficients always add to 1.
lines: Vector equation of the plane is
r = (1−s−t)a + sb + tc,  s, t ∈ R

recall.must_convey: That the plane equation is r = (1−s−t)a + sb + tc with TWO parameters s and t.
accept: r equals one minus s minus t times a plus s b plus t c with two parameters
a plane needs two parameters so use one minus s minus t, s and t
the three coefficients add to one and there are two free parameters
rendu parameters kavali, one minus s minus t, s, t
write the three point form of the plane

steps.why: One parameter sweeps a line, two sweep a surface. The coefficients summing to 1 is what keeps every point on the plane through those three.
common_mistakes: Using one parameter and describing a line instead.
